title: You're Glowing Right Now
sources: The human body emits visible light (ultra-weak photon emission) about 1,000 times weaker than the naked eye can detect, imaged in total darkness with cooled ultra-sensitive CCD cameras (Kobayashi, Kikuchi & Okamura 2009, PLoS ONE 4(7): e6256, Tohoku Institute of Technology / Kyoto University)
The emission is linked to metabolism: free-radical reactions in cells produce excited molecules that release photons (Kobayashi et al. 2009)
The face glowed more than the body, with the cheeks brightest (Kobayashi et al. 2009)
Emission follows a daily rhythm: lowest around 10 a.m., highest around 4 p.m., then dimming (Kobayashi et al. 2009)
